newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips gain 1.12 pct on technical rebound.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips gain 1.12 pct on technical rebound.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip stocks extended a technical rebound from last Thursday, bouyed by a firmer Wall Street and institutional nibbling after last week's sharp falls, analysts said.
At 0203 GMT, the benchmark Composite index of 100 large-capitalised stocks was had risen by 12.34 points, 1.12 percent to 1,116.92.
"I'm wondering if it (the rebound) will last. Last week's rebound on Wall Street helped improve sentiment here," said Jonathan Duckett, an institutional dealer at Mohaiyani Securities.
Among the most active stocks, Ekran rose 15 cents to 5.80 ringgit, while Renong gained two cents to 3.74 ringgit.

"(Ekran chairman) Ting Peck Khiing's confirmation last week that the Bakun (hydro-electric dam's stock listing) will have some foreign participation, allayed some fears over the stock," said Patrick Zecha, head of research at South Johor Securities.
"Renong had been oversold. It is fundamentally sound. It is still one of the country's main infrastructure-related companies," said Zecha.
At 0230 GMT volume stood at 59.5 million shares traded, valued at 373 million ringgit.
